jei.reikos_weather.barometer: Right-click for the weather, wind, season, forecast and storms on the way. While you hold it, a forecast panel shows in the corner of the screen.
jei.reikos_weather.umbrella: Hold it to block hailstones. Hold it while falling and you drift down gently, with no fall damage.
jei.reikos_weather.winter_coat: Keeps you warm: you can't freeze in it, and it adds a lot of warmth in the cold. It's far too warm for a heatwave, though.
jei.reikos_weather.goggles: Storm goggles let you see much further through sandstorms, blizzards and other thick weather.
jei.reikos_weather.thermometer: Hold it to see the air temperature and how warm or cold you feel. Weather, season, biome, height, time of day, clothing and nearby fires all count. Right-click for a reading in chat.
jei.reikos_weather.handheld_radar: Right-click to open a radar scope centred on you. It shows storm cells colour-coded by type, which way they are heading, when they will reach you, and nearby tornadoes. Scroll to zoom.
jei.reikos_weather.cloud_seeding_rocket: Fire it straight up under an open sky. Where it bursts, a rain cloud forms and drifts with the wind. Sometimes it grows into a thunderstorm.
jei.reikos_weather.weather_station: Outputs a redstone signal about the weather. Right-click to switch between precipitation, storm danger, wind, a 0-15 weather code and the season.
jei.reikos_weather.tornado_siren: Wails and powers redstone while a tornado or waterspout is within 160 blocks.
jei.reikos_weather.rain_barrel: Fills up with rainwater when it rains on it. Take the water out with a bucket when it's full, or with glass bottles.
jei.reikos_weather.weather_radar: Right-click to open the radar scope. Comparators read a signal that rises as the nearest storm gets closer (15 = overhead).
jei.reikos_weather.weather_vane: Turns to point into the wind. A comparator reads the wind direction: 1 = north, 2 = north-east... 8 = north-west (0 = no reading).
jei.reikos_weather.windmill: Turns into the wind and gives off a redstone signal as strong as the wind. It works best high up and out in the open, and turns slowly even on calm days.
jei.reikos_weather.weather_altar: End-game weather control. Right-click it with an offering to change the weather: sunflower (clear), water bucket (rain), lightning rod (thunderstorm), snow block (snow), packed ice (blizzard), ice (ice storm), blaze powder (heatwave), feather (gale), sand (sandstorm), cobweb (fog), ghast tear (supercell) or heart of the sea (hurricane). It needs time to recover between uses.
item.reikos_weather.hot_cocoa.tooltip: Warms you right through (about 10 °C, for three minutes)
item.reikos_weather.melon_cooler.tooltip: Cools you down in the heat (about 10 °C, for three minutes)
item.reikos_weather.salt.tooltip: Use it to melt ice glaze, snow, icicles and thin ice nearby

advancement.reikos_weather.rainmaker.des: Seed a rain cloud with a cloud seeding rocket
advancement.reikos_weather.weather_wizar: Change the weather at a weather altar
advancement.reikos_weather.fulgurite.des: Watch lightning fuse sand into glass
advancement.reikos_weather.ash_storm.des: Stand out in a Nether ash storm

jei.reikos_weather.hot_cocoa: A hot drink that warms you by about 10 °C for three minutes. Just the thing in a blizzard.
jei.reikos_weather.melon_cooler: An icy drink that cools you by about 10 °C for three minutes. Just the thing in a heatwave.
jei.reikos_weather.sun_hat: A wide straw hat that keeps the sun off: up to 6 °C cooler out in the sunshine.
jei.reikos_weather.tent: Place it like a bed. Sleeping in it skips the night but never moves your spawn point, and while you're inside you're sheltered from the weather and warmer.
jei.reikos_weather.salt: Use it on the ground to melt ice glaze, snow, icicles and thin ice around that spot. Water cauldrons drying out in a heatwave leave salt behind, or you can smelt a water bottle.
jei.reikos_weather.sandbag: Flood water from flash floods and hurricane storm surges can't reach within two blocks of a sandbag.
jei.reikos_weather.lightning_battery: Stores lightning that strikes within a few blocks (put a lightning rod over it), up to four charges. A redstone signal releases one charge as a strong two-second pulse out of the front. Comparators read how full it is.
jei.reikos_weather.forecast_board: Hang it on a wall to see the weather, the season and the next three forecasts at a glance.
jei.reikos_weather.storm_probe: Set it down in a tornado's path. A tornado passing nearby gives one piece of storm data; one passing right over it gives three. Break it to collect them. Meteorologists pay well for storm data.
jei.reikos_weather.storm_data: Readings from a storm probe. Trade it to a meteorologist villager.
jei.reikos_weather.meteorite: Left behind by meteors that fall on meteor shower nights. Mine it for iron, gold and sometimes a diamond.
report.reikos_weather.microclimate.valle: a sheltered valley (calmer, foggy at dawn)
report.reikos_weather.microclimate.rain_: the rain shadow of the mountains (drier)

jei.reikos_weather.leaf_pile: In autumn, fallen leaves pile up under trees. Wade through them, land in a deep pile to soften a fall, or gather them with a rake to compost. They rot away over the winter.
jei.reikos_weather.fallen_branch: Derechos, hurricanes and supercells break branches off trees. Clear them away for sticks, or leave them to rot after a few days.
jei.reikos_weather.icebox: Food kept in an icebox never spoils, however hot it gets. (A chest or barrel with ice, packed ice, blue ice or snow next to it works too.)
jei.reikos_weather.rice: Sometimes found in the grass of jungles, savannas and swamps. Plant it on farmland: it grows fast in the rain and during the monsoon, keeps going next to water, and stalls in dry weather.
jei.reikos_weather.kale: Sometimes found in the grass of cold places. A hardy winter green: frost doesn't hurt it and it keeps growing through the winter, but it slows right down in the heat.
jei.reikos_weather.winter_stew: A hearty stew that warms you up from the inside (Warmth for a minute and a half).
jei.reikos_weather.earthworm: Worms come up after rain: dig grass or dirt while it's wet for a good chance of finding some. Hold them in your off hand when you cast to bait the hook (fish bite sooner, and better ones).
jei.reikos_weather.stormfish: Bites in thunderstorms, supercells, hurricanes and derechos. Cooked, it gives a burst of Haste.
jei.reikos_weather.icefish: Bites when you fish through a hole in the ice in winter or in the cold. Cooked, it cools you down.
jei.reikos_weather.rake: Use it on the ground to gather the leaf piles (and branches) in a 5x5 area.
jei.reikos_weather.ice_saw: Cuts whole blocks of ice, packed ice and blue ice out of frozen lakes, ready to pack around your food.
jei.reikos_weather.paraglider: Hold use while falling to open it. Glide where you look; the wind carries you, and warm air rising off lava, fires, campfires, sun-baked sand and windy ridges lifts you up. No fall damage while gliding.
jei.reikos_weather.weather_radio: Keep it in your inventory and it warns you about storms closing in, tornadoes, dangerous weather on the way, extreme cold and heat, and blood moons, meteor showers and geomagnetic storms. Use it to switch it on or off; sneak and use it for a bulletin.

jei.reikos_weather.volcanic_ash:
Settles out of the ash cloud that drifts downwind of an erupting volcano, up to three layers deep, and dusts the lower slopes of volcanoes. Rain slowly washes it into the soil.

Use it on a crop to fertilize it like bone meal, or place it in layers like snow. Two ash make a bone meal.
jei.reikos_weather.sulfur: Mined from sulfur crust around volcanic vents and craters. Grind it with charcoal and bone meal into gunpowder.
jei.reikos_weather.sulfur_crust: Yellow crust found around steam vents and on the rims of volcanoes. Drops sulfur (Fortune helps; Silk Touch keeps the block).
jei.reikos_weather.volcanic_vent: A fumarole on a volcano's upper slopes, hissing hot steam. Scalding to stand on unless you sneak, and gives off warmth. Silk Touch to take one home.
jei.reikos_weather.seismograph: Feels the ground shake under a volcano that's waking up. Gives a redstone signal while a volcano within 1024 blocks rumbles (rising as the eruption nears and the closer it is), up to 15 during an eruption, and a little during the aftershocks.
tooltip.reikos_weather.seismograph: Redstone signal from nearby volcanic tremors

jei.reikos_weather.geyser: The vent of a geyser, found in hot springs. Every few minutes it erupts, throwing anything above it high into the air (and lifting a paraglider). A comparator reads 15 while it erupts. Silk Touch picks one up.
jei.reikos_weather.salt_crust: The white crust of a desert salt flat. Mine it for salt (Fortune helps; Silk Touch keeps the block).
jei.reikos_weather.black_sand: Volcanic sand from the shores of volcanic islands. Smelts into glass like any sand.

report.reikos_weather.foehn: A warm, dry föhn wind is blowing down off the mountains, and the snow is melting fast.
report.reikos_weather.frost_hollow: Cold air is pooling in this hollow tonight: expect a hard frost.

jei.reikos_weather.cracked_mud: The baked, cracked bed of a pond that dried up in a drought. Rain soaks it back into mud (and when the drought is over, the pond fills up again).
jei.reikos_weather.desert_dust: Dust blown far from a sandstorm, settled out of the haze. Rain washes it away. Like volcanic ash, it's good for the soil: use it on a crop.
jei.reikos_weather.peat: Cut from peat bogs. A slow-burning furnace fuel. Lightning (or fire) can set it smouldering, and a peat fire creeps slowly through the ground until it burns out or water puts it out.
reikos_weather.configuration.twilightBan: Earth's Shadow and the Belt of Venus
message.reikos_weather.microburst: Microburst! A violent downdraft is slamming into the ground.
message.reikos_weather.heat_burst: A heat burst: a sudden blast of hot, dry wind out of the dying storm.
message.reikos_weather.earthquake_strong: A strong earthquake! Get away from cliffs and glass.
message.reikos_weather.tsunami_warning: The sea is drawing back from the shore. A tsunami is coming: get to high ground now!
message.reikos_weather.calving: With a roar, a great slab of ice breaks off the glacier and crashes into the sea.
advancement.reikos_weather.fire_whirl.de: See a fire whirl spin up out of a wildfire
advancement.reikos_weather.blowhole.desc: Get thrown into the air by a blowhole
jei.reikos_weather.quicksand: Sand so waterlogged it can't take your weight, found on tidal flats, deltas, salt marshes, oasis shores and the beds of dry washes. You sink in to about your waist and can barely move. Sneak to work your way out slowly.
jei.reikos_weather.blowhole: The mouth of a shaft leading down into a sea cave, found on top of chalk cliffs. When a wave surges into the cave below, it booms and blasts a plume of spray into the air, higher in rough seas and at high tide. Stand on it if you dare. It needs sea water at the bottom of the shaft.
jei.reikos_weather.limestone: A pale sedimentary rock, found in limestone pavements, tower karst and tufa lakes.
reikos_weather.configuration.swell: Swell, Rogue Waves and Sea Foam
message.reikos_weather.rip_current: A rip current is pulling you out to sea! Swim along the shore to get out of it.
message.reikos_weather.tidal_bore: The tidal bore is coming up the river!
message.reikos_weather.glacial_outburst: The glacial lake has burst through its moraine! A flood is coming down the valley!
message.reikos_weather.landspout_warning: Landspout! A thin tornado has touched down nearby.
report.reikos_weather.year.wet: It's a wet year: more rain and storms than usual, and fewer droughts.
report.reikos_weather.year.dry: It's a dry year: droughts and heatwaves are likelier, and the rain is scarcer.
commands.reikos_weather.tornado.steam_de: A steam devil rises off the water
advancement.reikos_weather.rip_current.d: Get pulled out to sea by a rip current
advancement.reikos_weather.tidal_bore.de: Ride a tidal bore up a river in a boat
advancement.reikos_weather.maelstrom.des: Get dragged into the middle of a whirlpool
advancement.reikos_weather.outburst.desc: Be there when a glacial lake bursts through its moraine
jei.reikos_weather.petrified_wood: Wood from an ancient forest, turned to stone grain by grain by minerals in the groundwater. Found as fallen logs in the badlands' petrified forests.
jei.reikos_weather.pumice: Volcanic glass so full of gas bubbles it floats. Rafts of it drift on the sea after undersea eruptions, and it crusts the tops of obsidian flows.
message.reikos_weather.frost_quake: Boom! The frozen ground just cracked (a frost quake).
message.reikos_weather.seiche: With the wind gone, the lake is sloshing from shore to shore (a seiche).

advancement.reikos_weather.great_comet.d: See a bright comet in a dark sky
advancement.reikos_weather.fox_wedding.d: Be out in a sun shower, with the sun low enough for a rainbow
advancement.reikos_weather.struck_tree.d: See lightning blast the bark off a tree
advancement.reikos_weather.bolt_from_the: Nearly get hit by lightning out of a clear sky, miles from the storm

advancement.reikos_weather.blowdown.desc: See a gale tear a tree out of the ground, roots and all
advancement.reikos_weather.frost_quake.d: Hear the ground crack in a hard frost
advancement.reikos_weather.ice_shove.des: See the wind drive lake ice up onto the shore
advancement.reikos_weather.seiche.desc: Watch a lake slosh up its shore after a gale
advancement.reikos_weather.upwelling.des: Catch extra fish where cold water wells up off the coast
advancement.reikos_weather.vernal_pool.d: Find a vernal pool brimming in the spring
jei.reikos_weather.gypsum_sand: Brilliant white sand of gypsum crystals, the same mineral as plaster. It piles into dunes round the dry lakes it blows off.
jei.reikos_weather.shell_sand: Pale sand made almost entirely of broken shells, found on some beaches.
jei.reikos_weather.olivine_sand: Olive-green sand of olivine (peridot) crystals, worn out of the volcanic rock behind the beach.
jei.reikos_weather.pink_sand: Coral-pink sand: white sand tinted by the crushed red shells of tiny sea creatures.
jei.reikos_weather.rock_salt: Solid salt from deep salt beds, squeezed up to the surface in salt domes and flowing down their sides in salt glaciers.
